auditor: Principal Cloud Infrastructure & Financial Operations Engineer

measured_hardware_reality.note: Phase 14.7 executed entirely on local Apple Silicon M2 hardware with zero external cloud billing.

discrepancy_08_reconciliation.audit_finding: Identified mathematical divergence between pure active-inference seconds ($44 for 250k jobs) and 24/7 dedicated node cluster reservations ($1,485.60/mo).
discrepancy_08_reconciliation.explanation: In Phase 14.6, the report stated both '$0.000176 unit cost ($44 for 250k jobs)' and '$1,485.60/month dedicated cluster spend' without reconciling them. The $0.000176 figure represented purely active GPU computation seconds (0.044s * $0.004/s on ephemeral containers), ignoring idle standing reservations. When paying for a dedicated 2-node AWS cluster ($1,509.76/month), the actual cost per asset at 250,000 monthly jobs is $1,509.76 / 250,000 = $0.006039 (34.3x higher). At low utilization, standing dedicated nodes are wasteful; serverless execution is vastly superior until volume reaches several million requests per month.

production_recommendation: Adopt Serverless GPU execution (Modal or RunPod Serverless) for launch through 100k users. Serverless achieves $82.50/month at 100k users vs $1,509.76/month on dedicated standing nodes (18.3x savings). Transition to dedicated reserved instances only when persistent monthly volume surpasses 10.5 million try-on assets.
